title: Add dashboards + alerts for retention enforcement (lag, errors, delete volume, bloat risk)
author: Caleb Johnson
description: Context: Retention enforcement workers are landing for audit logs + selected telemetry datasets. We need baseline visibility + paging coverage before we ramp rollout beyond canary tenants. This PR adds Grafana dashboards and Prometheus alert rules for retention enforcement jobs across Hosted/Dedicated/Private (where metrics are exported), focusing on: (1) lag/backlog (how far behind enforcement is), (2) error rate and retry behavior, (3) delete volume/throughput (are we actually deleting), and (4) storage bloat indicators (when deletion is falling behind growth). Scope: adds a new dashboard folder "Retention Enforcement" with two dashboards (Overview + Datastore detail), creates alert rules with conservative defaults and environment overrides, wires annotations to include tenant_id/environment/region labels, and adds a short README with links to the runbook and suggested oncall responses. Notes: This depends on retention worker metrics introduced in redwood PR-18491 (metrics names + label schema). For Private, the dashboards assume the customer has wired metrics scrape; alerts are gated behind enable_private_rules=false by default. Rollout: dashboards are safe; alert rules are disabled in prod by default and enabled via per-env values after a 48h observation window. Related: ENG-2944, Confluence runbook "retention-enforcement-job-runbook".
commits: Add retention enforcement dashboard folder + overview dashboard
Add datastore-specific dashboard (audit logs) with lag + delete throughput panels
Add Prometheus alert rules for lag/error/delete-stall + bloat indicators
Add per-environment values + disablement switches for Private deployments
Docs: add README with metric definitions and oncall response guidance
conversation: Reviewer (Sean Gallagher): Can we avoid paging on short spikes in delete errors? We saw transient timeouts during the incident last week; suggest using 15m window and requiring >N failures. Author (Caleb Johnson): Updated RetentionEnforcementDeleteErrorsHigh to use rate() over 15m with a minimum volume gate (delete_attempts_total > 200) and added a non-paging warning for smaller tenants. Reviewer (Allison Grant): Please align alert labels with our conventions (service, severity, runbook_url) and add a clear runbook link. Author: Done; added runbook_url to each alert and set service=retention-enforcement. Reviewer (Logan Wright): For telemetry datasets, "bloat" is more about partition TTL not being applied; can we make the dashboard query generic (table label) without implying deletes? Author: Adjusted panel copy to "data expiration" and added a note that enforcement may be TTL-based depending on datastore; retained delete volume panels only on audit log dashboard. Reviewer (Kevin Osei): Confirm we’re not exposing tenant_id in shared Grafana for internal-only? Author: tenant_id is included as a label for internal clusters; dashboards default to grouping by environment/region, and tenant_id requires an explicit variable selection. Approved after changes. Approvals: Sean Gallagher ✅, Allison Grant ✅, Logan Wright ✅, Kevin Osei ✅.
alert_rules_added: RetentionEnforcementLagHigh (page) - enforcement watermark behind by >6h for 30m (env-tuned)
RetentionEnforcementLagRisingFast (warning) - lag slope indicates catching up unlikely
RetentionEnforcementDeleteErrorsHigh (page) - elevated delete failure rate with volume gate
RetentionEnforcementNoDeletesObserved (warning) - attempts present but deletes_total flat (possible misconfig or hold)
RetentionEnforcementDatastoreBloatRisk (page) - storage growth outpacing expirations / lag increasing
dashboard_panels_highlights: Queue/backlog depth (if exported) and processing rate
P95/Max delete batch duration (proxy for DB pain)
Storage growth vs expiration throughput (bloat risk indicator)
release_notes: Internal: Adds Retention Enforcement dashboards and (disabled-by-default) alerting rules for retention enforcement jobs. Enable prod paging rules after 48h baseline observation; see README/retention-enforcement.md for thresholds and runbook links.
